## What the player hears

The race engineer calls 'Limiter On' as the player enters the pit lane, 'Go' as the player is released from the pit box, and 'Limiter Off - clear of pit lane' crossing the exit line. PWS_PIT09 ('Gear') fires natively in vanilla play and needed no code - its trigger condition is unidentified (low priority, see docs/TRIAGE_NOTES.txt).

## Why it was silent

Traced 4+ full live pit-stop cycles (tools/trace_pitstop_full.py) to confirm the veh+0x3450 pittingStatus enum end to end (0=track, 1=driving, 2=entering pit lane, 3=stopped in box, 4=exiting) and fire on its 1->2/3->4/4->0 edges through the same InsertDriverTableEntry pipeline used by traffic_density_commentary. First build used the wrong eid (a column mix-up in the low-eid twin lookup) - it compiled clean and the queue-head readback even confirmed the eid landed, yet it played 'Gear' both times. Caught by isolation-testing each candidate eid alone with tools/commentary_inject.py before trusting the DLL again - now a standing rule in this folder's CLAUDE.md. Two more bugs found after that: injecting on every retry attempt caused genuine double-plays (fixed: fire once, only poll to confirm), and waiting for audio silence before firing delivered 'Go' too late (fixed: fire immediately on the trigger edge). Full methodology: docs/PITSTOP_METHODOLOGY.md.

## Evidence

findings.jsonl (~10 entries this session, incl. the eid mix-up, the double-fire bug, and the late-fire bug). pit_exit_log.txt shows timestamp-confirmed fires on all three edges; user-confirmed audible for all three clips.

## Additional code

The byte change alone is not enough for this feature — see
`pit_exit_commentary.c` in this folder, copied from
`dll/pit_exit_commentary.c`. Read `dll/README.md` before modifying it;
it documents traps found across earlier iterations.

## Rebuild

```bash
C:\msys64\mingw32\bin\gcc.exe -shared -O2 -Wall \
    -o pit_exit_commentary.dll pit_exit_commentary.c -lkernel32
```

`source.c` writes the same bytes the manifest would write to the .exe,
but into the running process at DLL attach — so no game file is
modified and not loading the DLL is the uninstall. Each site verifies
its expected original bytes first and skips on mismatch, so a different
game build is a no-op rather than a corruption.
